title: Following Louis wherever he played
summary: Cootie went to hear Louis whenever he could and was interested in no one else; he says Louis played best with Les Hite's band.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Would you -- I mean, did you -- if he happened to be playing in town where you were playing in town, did you usually go by and try to catch him?
Oh, yeah. Any time I got the chance to hear Louis Armstrong, I was there.
No kidding. You mean for years, Cootie?

Is that right? Isn't that marvelous? That's terrific. Well, let me ask you something. Did you -- did you think it was too bad that maybe he didn't always have the kind of background that maybe he would have profited by?
I wasn't interested in nobody but Louis.
You didn't care. Well, nevertheless, I mean Louis played better when he had guys with him that felt --
-- well, for instance, when he had a big band in back of him, say like Luis Louie Russell's band or something.
I mean, he wasn't maybe getting just the background that was as helpful as it might be.
But, of course, he didn't really need it, it's true. He didn't really need anything, did he?
I think he played the greatest with Hite's Les Hight's band in California.
That's with Lionel Hampton, and Lawrence Hite's Brown was with Les Hight's band. That was his peak.
Well, that's about 1928. No, wait a minute.
Oh, I see. Yeah, he wasn't -- he didn't -- that didn't last very long did it?
Yeah. Sebastian's Cotton Club. He used to work out there.
I think it was a lot longer than that.
Was it really. I didn't realize that.
Well, then, did some of those -- some of those records -- were some of those records made with that band?
